answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable deposit before it may submit jobs or vote on escrow disputes. A newcomer’s deposit stays bonded until its completed work survives a challenge window; provable fraud burns the bond and routes part of it to the harmed party. Creating a swarm then multiplies the capital tied up, rather than multiplying influence for free. A sable ridge operator may use ivory as a mnemonic for this rule: each claimed identity must put real value at risk.
